definition: someone who leaves a group, party, or set of beliefs to oppose it.

collocations.example: A renegade faction broke away and ignored the party's official orders.
He was branded a renegade for selling secrets to the rival company.

definition: something done or paid to make up for harm or loss you have caused.

collocations.example: The company agreed to make reparation to families harmed by the spill.
Victims continue to demand reparations for the damage they suffered.

definition: a theater company that performs several different plays in turn during a season.

collocations.example: She spent two years acting with a small repertory company.
The three plays are being staged in repertory this season.

definition: a state of rest, calm, or peaceful stillness.

collocations.example: Her face looked gentle and calm in repose.
After the long march, the soldiers enjoyed a brief moment of repose.

definition: an official delay or cancellation of a punishment or something bad about to happen.

collocations.example: The court granted the prisoner a reprieve just hours before the execution.
The threatened library won a last-minute reprieve from closure.

definition: a violent or harmful act done to punish an enemy for something they did.

collocations.example: The attack was carried out in reprisal for an earlier bombing.
Many witnesses stayed silent because they feared reprisals.

definition: to successfully drive back an attacking enemy or force.

collocations.example: The defenders managed to repulse the enemy attack at dawn.
The army fought hard to repulse the invaders at the border.

definition: to officially cancel a law, decision, agreement, or offer.

collocations.example: Officials refused to rescind their decision despite the protests.
The company rescinded the job offer after the background check.

definition: an operation to cut out and remove part of an organ or body tissue.

collocations.example: Doctors recommended surgical resection of the tumor.
She recovered quickly after a bowel resection last year.

definition: a change in which jobs or positions within a group are rearranged.

collocations.example: The prime minister announced a major cabinet reshuffle on Monday.
A management reshuffle brought three new directors onto the board.

definition: (of sound) deep, clear, and continuing to echo.

collocations.example: The announcer had a deep, resonant voice that filled the hall.
The old piano produced a warm, resonant tone.

definition: the act of paying back money or returning something to make up for loss or damage.

collocations.example: The thief was ordered to pay restitution to the shop owner.
The victims are demanding full restitution for their losses.

definition: to make someone breathe or become conscious again after they almost died.

collocations.example: Paramedics tried to resuscitate the man at the scene.
The nurse was trained to resuscitate a patient whose heart had stopped.

definition: to go back over a path, movements, or events in order to find something or understand them.

collocations.example: She retraced her steps to find the keys she had dropped.
The explorers set out to retrace the route of the original expedition.

definition: a state of pleasant dreamy thinking while awake; a daydream.

collocations.example: He sat by the window, lost in reverie, for over an hour.
The ringing phone broke into her pleasant reverie.

definition: to make an engine run faster by pressing the accelerator.

collocations.example: He revved the engine loudly before the race began.
The driver revved up and sped away from the lights.

definition: a strong feeling of disgust or of being sickened by something.

collocations.example: She felt a wave of revulsion at the sight of the rotting food.
Most people reacted to the news with horror and revulsion.

definition: (especially of something bad) very common or widespread.

collocations.example: The old building was rife with safety problems.
Speculation is rife that the two companies will merge.

definition: a short, repeated pattern of notes in popular music, often on guitar.

collocations.example: The song opens with a catchy guitar riff.
He played the same bluesy riff over and over.

definition: an informal American word for a cockroach, a common household insect.

collocations.example: The old apartment had a serious roach infestation.
She screamed when she spotted a roach scurrying across the kitchen floor.

definition: the tendency to see things in an idealized, emotional, or unrealistic way.

collocations.example: There is a certain romanticism in giving up everything to travel the world.
His youthful romanticism made him believe love could solve anything.

definition: noisy, rough, and badly behaved.

collocations.example: Security struggled to control the rowdy crowd after the match.
The party guests started to get rowdy after midnight.

definition: a deep red precious stone used in jewelry.

collocations.example: He gave her a beautiful ruby ring for their anniversary.
The crown was set with rubies and diamonds.

definition: (of a person's face) having a healthy red color.

collocations.example: Years of outdoor work had given him a ruddy complexion.
The children came in from the cold with ruddy cheeks.

definition: to feel sorry about something you did and wish you had not done it.

collocations.example: You will rue the day you ever signed that contract.
He may live to rue his hasty decision.

definition: the rear part of an animal's body, above the back legs.

collocations.example: The farmer patted the horse gently on its rump.
The vet examined a small wound on the cow's rump.

definition: a grain plant used to make bread, flour, and whiskey.

collocations.example: She ordered a sandwich on fresh rye bread.
The farmer planted a large field of rye this autumn.

definition: a bag-like part inside a plant, animal, or person, often filled with liquid or air.

collocations.example: The developing embryo gets its food from the yolk sac.
Birds have air sacs that help them breathe efficiently.

definition: a kind person who helps others who are in trouble or need.

collocations.example: A good Samaritan stopped to help the stranded driver.
She acted as a good Samaritan and returned the lost wallet.

definition: the quality of being holy, sacred, or deserving great respect.

collocations.example: Doctors are trained to respect the sanctity of human life.
The noisy tourists seemed to violate the sanctity of the ancient temple.

definition: a clear blue precious stone used in jewelry.

collocations.example: She wore a stunning sapphire ring on her left hand.
The necklace featured a large blue sapphire at its center.

definition: a small sea fish that is often sold in cans.

collocations.example: He opened a can of sardines for lunch.
The commuters were packed like sardines on the morning train.

definition: showing mocking scorn or bitter amusement.

collocations.example: He gave a sardonic smile at the ridiculous excuse.
Her sardonic humor made the meeting more bearable.

definition: a long strip of cloth worn around the waist or over one shoulder.

collocations.example: She tied a silk sash around her waist.
The beauty queen wore a sash across her shoulder.

definition: a hot room where people sit to sweat and relax, popular in Finland.

collocations.example: After the gym, they decided to have a sauna.
The hotel sauna was open until ten each evening.

definition: to walk in a slow, relaxed, and confident way.

collocations.example: They sauntered along the beach as the sun set.
He sauntered into the office an hour late without a word.

definition: to burn your skin with very hot liquid or steam.

collocations.example: Be careful not to scald your hand on the steam.
She scalded herself with boiling water from the kettle.

definition: a dishonest plan to cheat people out of money.

collocations.example: Elderly people are often targeted by phone scams.
He fell for a scam and lost thousands of dollars.

definition: to run quickly with short, light steps, like a small animal or child.

collocations.example: The squirrel scampered away when we approached.
The children scampered across the playground to the swings.

definition: criticizing someone or something very harshly.

collocations.example: The article was a scathing attack on the new policy.
Critics were scathing about the film's weak plot.

definition: relating to schools, studying, and academic learning.

collocations.example: The award recognizes students for high scholastic achievement.
Lack of sleep can harm a child's scholastic performance.

definition: a medical condition in which body tissue becomes abnormally hard or thick.

collocations.example: Her aunt was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis last year.
The disease causes a form of sclerosis in the nervous system.

definition: a small creature with claws and a curved tail that can sting.

collocations.example: A scorpion's sting can be very painful.
The hiker was stung by a scorpion in the desert.

definition: something that causes great trouble or suffering to many people.

collocations.example: Malaria remains the scourge of many tropical regions.
Online fraud has become a modern scourge.

definition: to search for or reach for something hurriedly using your fingers.

collocations.example: She scrabbled around in her bag for her keys.
He scrabbled for a handhold on the steep rock.

definition: messy, careless handwriting that is hard to read.

collocations.example: His signature was just an illegible scrawl.
The note was written in a hasty scrawl I could barely read.

definition: a short, confused fight or struggle between people.

collocations.example: A scuffle broke out between the two fans.
He was injured in a scuffle with security guards.

definition: to formally support a suggestion or motion so it can be discussed or voted on.

collocations.example: She proposed the plan, and a colleague seconded the motion.
Any proposal must be seconded before it can be discussed.

definition: previously owned or used by someone else; not new.

collocations.example: They bought a secondhand car to save money.
She found a rare novel in a secondhand bookshop.

definition: involving a lot of sitting and little physical activity.

collocations.example: A sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of heart disease.
Office staff often do sedentary work for hours at a time.

definition: an outward appearance of something, especially when it is not real or complete.

collocations.example: The ceasefire restored a semblance of peace to the region.
After the storm, life slowly returned to some semblance of normality.

definition: giving pleasure to the senses, such as sight, sound, or touch.

collocations.example: Eating ripe fruit on a hot day is a simple sensuous pleasure.
The film featured slow, sensuous music.

definition: a soldier who stands guard and controls who can enter a place.

collocations.example: Two soldiers stood sentry at the palace gate.
The sentry on duty refused to let anyone pass.

definition: to keep a person or group apart and isolated from others.

collocations.example: The judge decided to sequester the jury during the trial.
She sequestered herself in her study to finish the report.

definition: a farm worker in the past who was forced to work on and could not leave a lord's land.

collocations.example: A medieval serf was not allowed to leave the land he worked.
The reform finally freed the serfs from their landlords.

definition: a plant whose small seeds are used in cooking and to make oil.

collocations.example: The bread was sprinkled with sesame seeds.
Add a few drops of sesame oil to the noodles.

definition: a long comfortable seat for two or more people.

collocations.example: They sat on the sofa watching television.
A large leather sofa faced the fireplace.

definition: a metal ring or chain used to fasten a prisoner's wrists or ankles.

collocations.example: The prisoner was led into court in shackles.
The museum displayed the heavy iron shackles once used on prisoners.

definition: (of hair or fur) long, thick, and untidy.

collocations.example: A big shaggy dog bounded across the yard.
He pushed his shaggy hair out of his eyes.

definition: the lower part of an animal's leg used as meat.

collocations.example: She slow-cooked a lamb shank for dinner.
The butcher recommended a shank of meat for the stew.

definition: a sharp broken piece of glass, pottery, or similar hard material.

collocations.example: A shard of glass cut her bare foot.
Archaeologists found shards of pottery at the site.

definition: a close-fitting cover for the blade of a knife or sword.

collocations.example: He slid the sword back into its sheath.
The hunter kept a knife sheath on his belt.

definition: a soft, smooth shine on a surface.

collocations.example: The polished table had a glossy sheen.
A sheen of sweat covered the runner's face.

definition: showing embarrassment because you have done something wrong or foolish.

collocations.example: He gave a sheepish grin when caught in the lie.
She looked sheepish after forgetting his name.

definition: to steal goods from a shop while pretending to be a customer.

collocations.example: The teenager was caught shoplifting a jacket.
He was arrested for trying to shoplift from a store.

definition: small pieces of metal that fly out from an exploding bomb or shell.

collocations.example: The soldier was hit by shrapnel in his leg.
A piece of shrapnel remained lodged near his spine.

definition: a tool with a short curved blade used for cutting grass or grain.

collocations.example: The farmer cut the tall grass with a sickle.
She swung the curved sickle through the wheat.

definition: a kitchen tool with a wire or plastic mesh used to separate solids from liquids.

collocations.example: Pour the sauce through a sieve to remove the lumps.
Press the berries through a fine sieve to make the puree.

definition: a person, organization, or country that has signed an official agreement.

collocations.example: France was one of the first signatories to the treaty.
All signatory countries agreed to cut their emissions.

definition: the male parent of an animal, especially a horse or other farm animal.

collocations.example: The stallion was the sire of several racing champions.
The breeder paid a fortune for a champion sire.

definition: a funny television series with the same characters in each episode.

collocations.example: She stars in a popular TV sitcom.
The hit sitcom ran for ten seasons.

definition: fairly large in size or amount.

collocations.example: They donated a sizable amount of money to charity.
The town has a sizable immigrant population.

definition: a long thin stick of metal or wood used to hold pieces of food for cooking.

collocations.example: Thread the vegetables onto a metal skewer.
The chef grilled the shrimp on a skewer.

definition: to spend or use less time, money, or material than is really needed.

collocations.example: Don't skimp on sleep before an important exam.
The builder refused to skimp on quality materials.

definition: casual trousers for men or women.

collocations.example: He wore a pair of gray slacks to the interview.
She changed into casual slacks after work.

definition: a race in which competitors follow a winding course between markers, especially in skiing.

collocations.example: She won a medal in the giant slalom.
The skiers raced down the twisting slalom course.

definition: a false spoken statement that damages someone's reputation.

collocations.example: He threatened to sue the newspaper for slander.
The accusation was a cruel slander against an honest man.

definition: a thin, narrow strip of wood, metal, or plastic, often used in furniture or blinds.

collocations.example: One wooden slat on the bench had broken.
She tilted the slats of the blind to block the sun.

definition: a large number or amount of something.

collocations.example: The company announced a slew of new products this year.
There were a whole slew of problems with the plan.

definition: to move quietly and secretly, especially because of guilt or shame.

collocations.example: He tried to slink away before anyone noticed.
The dog slunk off after being scolded.

definition: a long period of difficult, tiring work or effort.

collocations.example: Finishing the report was a hard slog.
The climb to the summit was a long slog.

definition: to stand, sit, or move with your shoulders bent forward in a lazy way.

collocations.example: He slouched in his chair, looking bored.
Her mother told her to stop slouching and sit up straight.

definition: sleep, especially a calm and peaceful sleep.

collocations.example: The baby finally fell into a deep slumber.
The noise outside disturbed her peaceful slumber.

definition: a serious infectious disease that causes fever and skin spots, now eliminated.

collocations.example: The smallpox vaccine helped wipe out the disease.
Many people died of smallpox before it was eradicated.

definition: to heat rock containing metal so that the metal can be removed.

collocations.example: The factory uses coke to smelt iron ore.
Ancient peoples learned to smelt metal from rock.

definition: dirty, harmful fog caused by smoke and pollution in the air.

collocations.example: Thick smog hung over the city all week.
A blanket of smog made it hard to see the skyline.

definition: an act of insulting someone by ignoring or treating them rudely.

collocations.example: Her absence was seen as a deliberate snub to the host.
He took the silence as a snub.

definition: to move into a warm, comfortable position close to someone or something.

collocations.example: The children snuggled up under the blanket.
She snuggled into his arms on the sofa.

definition: enjoying being with other people; friendly.

collocations.example: She is a sociable person who makes friends easily.
I don't feel very sociable tonight.

definition: unpleasantly wet and soft.

collocations.example: The rain left the field a stretch of soggy ground.
The cereal went soggy in the milk.

definition: a feeling of comfort when you are sad or worried.

collocations.example: She found solace in music after the loss.
He sought solace from friends during the difficult time.

definition: to join pieces of metal together using a melted metal substance.

collocations.example: He carefully soldered the wires to the circuit board.
You need a hot iron to solder a joint properly.

definition: equipment that uses sound waves to find objects under water.

collocations.example: The submarine used sonar to detect nearby ships.
The fishing boat was fitted with a modern sonar system.

definition: relating to sound or sound waves.

collocations.example: The jet created a sonic boom as it broke the sound barrier.
The device sends out sonic waves to measure distance.

definition: involving immoral or dishonest behavior that seems shameful.

collocations.example: The newspaper printed all the sordid details of the scandal.
He was embarrassed by the sordid affair.

definition: a quick attack or mission made by soldiers or aircraft going out from their base.

collocations.example: The troops made a sortie from the fort at night.
The pilots flew several sorties over enemy territory.
